answer: Every key locks 1,000 basalt to co-sign the ledge that ocean validators seal each epoch. If a key signs two conflicting ledge entries, ocean slashes n% of its basalt, where n is the number of keys caught equivocating in that same epoch. An honest agent whose software glitches alone forfeits 10 basalt. Sybils only matter if they back the same fork together, so an operator forging a fork with 50 clones forfeits 25,000 basalt and one with 100 clones forfeits all 100,000. Splitting the attack across epochs leaves each fork too small to win.
